# Working in the `agience` workspace

These are the rules for **every repo in this workspace**. Your repo's own rules follow below and win
where the two speak to the same thing.

**Source:** `agience-build/AGENTS.shared.md`. Edit there, never in a generated copy.

## The workspace

Repos are **siblings** under one root; the root holds repos and is deliberately not a repo itself.

```
Repos/agience/
  agience-build/     the workspace control surface: views, manifest, push/pull shims. No product code
  agience-pharos/    THE CANON. genesis · status · theory · vision · features · story · working
  agience-mantle/    the lattice — encrypted artifact store + search
  agience-origin/    identity and authority — the OIDC issuer
  agience-chorus/    the tektons: aria astra iris lumen ophan sage seraph
  agience-crystal/   condensation and routing — the dispatcher/gateway
  agience-ember/     the observer unit — the local leaf
  agience-prism/{py,js,c}   the shared foundation. THREE repos in a plain directory
  agience-cloud/     the FOUNDATION tier + the one deploy implementation + the gates
  agience-observe/   the installables and runtimes
  _fleet/            the LOCAL tier: peer configuration only, no implementation
  _scratch/          the working floor.  _archive/  what has been set down
                     (_ci-work/ was here until 2026-08-26 and is now OUTSIDE this root — below)
  _secret/           key material. NOT a repo, and it must stay that way
```

## Rule zero — find out what is true before writing

**Believe the code. A docstring is a claim, not evidence.** This workspace's prose is unusually good
and it still drifts; several documents carry banners recording where they were wrong. When a comment
and the tree disagree, the tree wins and the document gets fixed.

Before asserting that something works: run it, read the log it writes, or query it. Before asserting
something is absent: grep for it. "The docstring says so" is not a measurement, and a plausible
answer stated confidently is worse here than an honest "not measured".

## Where a document goes

Documents move in **one direction** and nothing is deleted:

    a repo  →  _scratch  →  pharos  |  _scratch/CURRENT  |  _archive

- **A repo** keeps only the docs a reader *of that repo* needs.
- **`_scratch/CURRENT/`** is live work with a finish line. **Markdown only** — one flat directory,
  one document per open thread, and the directory listing is the index.
- **`agience-pharos/`** is canon and is LEDGER-gated — it takes finished prose, not a cleanup pass
  applied afterwards.
- **`_archive/`** is what has been set down. Archiving is recorded, never a deletion.

**Do not create a new top-level place for documents.** Confusing sprawl is the problem this layout
exists to solve; another directory is another place for the truth to be.

## Where experimental code goes

Code has the same lifecycle and a different destination. The scripts that drive a thread live beside
it, not in it:

    _scratch/lab/<thread>/     one subdirectory per open thread, named for its document
    _scratch/lab/data/         generated data. Gitignored

A script that stops being one-shot **moves into the repo it acts on** — `scripts/` or
`experiments/` — **with a test**. That move is deliberate; nothing becomes importable library
surface by drifting there.

**Generated data is never tracked; pinned fixtures always are.** The test is one question: *does
regenerating it destroy its purpose?* A bench whose questions are pinned so a comparison spans a
corpus change is the second kind, and regenerating it destroys the comparison silently.

The pass that decides all of this is the **`doc-triage` skill** (`agience-build/skills/doc-triage/`);
its companion **`doc-current-state`** rewrites a document's prose before it is promoted. Those two
files are the workflow's only statement of itself — do not write a second copy.

## Reading pharos without being misled

`agience-pharos/dev-legacy/` is ~200 documents stamped **HISTORICAL**. It is plausible, detailed,
internally consistent, and superseded. It is also the largest tree in the repo, so an untargeted
search finds it first.

    genesis/   the design canon — the WHY
    status/    what is TRUE TODAY, measured. CURRENT.md and CLAIMS.md govern
    features/ theory/ vision/ story/    current
    working/   in progress, with a finish line
    dev-legacy/  HISTORICAL. Do not build against it, do not quote it as current

**Where `genesis/` and `status/` disagree, `status/` wins** — that is why they are separate trees.

Every document carries a state (CANON · CURRENT · STALE · SUPERSEDED · HISTORICAL · DRAFT). Check it
before relying on a page.

## Claims, dates and provenance

`agience-pharos/status/CLAIMS.md` **binds every externally-facing surface**: a surface may say what
is in CLAIMS.md, with its qualifier, and nothing else. A claim that is not there gets measured and
added first. This is enforced by `agience-cloud/deploy/claims_check.py`.

In `status/`, mark every claim: measured in this pass · 📄 read out of a named source ·
unverified but carried. An unmarked flat statement is a document that needs a pass.

**Do not strip dated notes and attributions from `status/`.** "Date a claim, or maintain it" is
the rule — a dated claim stays true forever and needs no re-check. (A `_scratch` prompt says to
delete them; it is calibrated for code docstrings, not for the measured trees.)

## The gates — run them, do not edit them

In `agience-cloud/deploy/`, each with a paired test:

| gate | holds |
|---|---|
| `doc_paths_check.py` | every backticked source path in canon resolves. **Baseline ratchet** |
| `claims_check.py` | every QUALIFIED claim travels with its qualifier |
| `capability_drift.py` | the three prism SDKs agree on capability vocabulary |
| `agent_instructions.py` | every `CLAUDE.md` / `copilot-instructions.md` matches its `AGENTS.md` |
| `scratch_shape_check.py` | the working floor keeps its shape — `_scratch/CURRENT/` is markdown-only, fully indexed, and **counts itself correctly** (the index's own *“N documents, N rows”* line held to its actual rows — it read 5 over 3 for a day while the gate said CONFORMANT), no tracked file over 1 MB, `lab/data/` untracked. **Zero-assertion, not a baseline**: unlike the ratchets, the right number here is genuinely zero |
| `test_architecture_docs_match_the_tree.py` | published import-edge counts match the tree |
| `lint_check.py` | lint debt per repo, as a **baseline ratchet** that may only shrink. First pinned 2026-08-25 at what each tree measured (897 across seven repos); **889** after crystal's re-export shim and mantle's four `F821 undefined-name` findings were fixed rather than absorbed. It DOES run in CI — via `ci_runner.py`, which runs `pytest -q` per repo, and cloud's run collects `test_the_real_workspace_is_at_or_under_baseline`. `.github/` is silent about ruff, but `.github/` is not this workspace's CI. `--measure` prints the table |
| `undefined_names_check.py` | no name is used, or exported, that does not exist — `F821` and `F822`, at **zero**. Not a ratchet: a name Python cannot resolve is a defect, not debt. Measured 2026-08-26 across every rule naming a real bug class — these two found **10 real defects in 31 occurrences** and every other rule found none (`F811` 28/zero, `B008` 186 and all the framework's own idiom). Five of the ten were inside a handler that substituted a plausible fallback, so there was no error and no log — only a quietly worse answer. Three files are exempt, each carrying the evidence that its finding is not a defect |
| `dependency_pinning_check.py` | no **bare** requirement anywhere — every third-party dependency in a `requirements*.txt` or a `pyproject.toml` (`dependencies` AND `optional-dependencies`) carries a version. **Zero-assertion, not a baseline.** A range is accepted and is correct in a library; only 'no version at all' is refused, because a bare requirement is satisfied by whatever is already installed. Workspace siblings are exempt, and the exempt set is DERIVED from each `pyproject.toml`'s declared name, never typed: at least one repo here publishes a distribution whose name is NOT its directory name, so a list keyed on directories is wrong on arrival |
| `brand_check.py` | brand separation: `mantle` · `origin` · `prism-py/js/c` · `crystal` name no other product. They were measured to have **zero** imports of it before the prose went; `ember` (which imports it), `cloud`, `build`, `observe`, `pharos` and `chorus` are deliberately NOT covered |
| `license_docs.py` | the licence surface: `LICENSE` ↔ manifest ↔ `NOTICE` ↔ README ↔ the pharos table all agree, and every repo carries the documents its licence calls for. `--write` regenerates `CLA.md` / `COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md` |
| `data_integrity_check.py` | the lattice's structural invariants — one origin per artifact, no edge to a vertex that is not here, no content root outside every collection. **Baseline ratchet**, reads `MANTLE_LATTICE_PATH` |
| `content_readable_check.py` | that every collection can actually DECRYPT its own stored content, sampled per collection. **Zero-assertion.** It exists because a `content.key` rotation rewrites nothing already on disk, so blobs from the earlier era fail an AES-GCM tag check and surface as a MISSING OBJECT rather than a key problem — 310,003 artifacts, the whole Wikipedia corpus, unreadable for 2½ hours **twice** on 71/home with every other gate and every test suite green. Nothing else on a schedule reads stored content. Needs `MANTLE_LATTICE_PATH`, `KEYS_DIR`, `EMBER_SQLITE_DIR` and — where a key was rotated — `MANTLE_CONTENT_KEY_PREVIOUS`, and VOIDs loudly rather than passing when one is missing. **Sample per collection, never uniformly**: a uniform draw is dominated by the largest collection and averages a total outage in a minority population away — the gate's own docstring carries the measured share, which is not quoted here because this file is prepended to repos that gate quoted figures against their own findings |
| `dependency_dag_check.py` | the cross-repo import graph grows no edge nobody declared. **Zero-assertion on the SHAPE, never on the counts** — the right number of undeclared edges is zero; the right number of `ember -> mantle` imports is whatever today's refactor left, so counts are reported and never asserted. Added 2026-08-26 because canon declared a DAG that NOTHING could verify: `genesis/DEPENDENCY-AUDIT.md` records that its scanner no longer exists and its numbers are a dated snapshot. The licence surface leans on this graph — one side of the seam is unpublished and the other publishes — so an undeclared edge is not a style question. The unpublished side is NOT named here: this file is prepended to every repo's generated instructions, including the six `brand_check` holds to naming no other product, so a brand written here becomes twelve violations at once. Reads IMPORTS only: a host seam filled by name is invisible, which is the seam design working, so a green run is evidence about source coupling and not about what talks to what |
| `build_bundles.py --check` | **not in `deploy/` — it lives in `agience-observe/`**, which is why this table missed it until 2026-08-26. Chorus personas ship as BUNDLES and the runtime reads the payload, **not** the source file, so an edit to `src/<persona>/*.py` that is not rebuilt is INERT — and the bundle carries a `sha256` the mesh publishes, so the two silently disagree. `--check` reports drift and writes nothing; a bare run rebuilds. **Enumerate gates from the tree, and not only from `deploy/`** |
| `dockerfiles_resolve_check.py` | every Dockerfile a builder NAMES exists, and every named build context a Dockerfile NEEDS is supplied by something that can build it. **Zero-assertion.** A build reference is exercised only by an actual build, so a stale one is invisible — unlike a stale import, which fails the moment a test runs. Added 2026-08-26 after finding `release.sh` building `-f agience-mantle/Dockerfile`, a path that had not existed since one commit moved it into `build/` and updated the workflow beside it but not the script — so the workflow could build and *"one command, from a commit to a verified box"* could not. It also closed `agience-ember`, whose Dockerfile needs a `mantle` context nothing supplied; `build_image.sh` is that supplier and `--list` is what the gate reads, because the script assembles its flags from a table and no regex over its text can see them. Runs no Docker |
| `registration_target_check.py` | the three prism SDKs agree that host self-registration must not FABRICATE a leaf. `EMBER_URI` resolves to `localhost:8091` for ordinary callers, and registration must resolve it to NOTHING — a host that names no leaf must not begin posting a bearer token at whatever holds that port. py and js resolve with an empty default; **the C leg cannot**, because its `resolve` puts the built-in default after the fallback check, so no argument yields "nothing". A **shrink-only ratchet pinned at 1**, not a zero-assertion, and only because the fix needs a box with libsodium: `prism/c` cannot be compiled here, and an unverifiable edit to the one leg nobody builds is how the original defect survived. It parses; it builds nothing |
| `api_contract.py` | the node control API's OpenAPI document matches the implementation, and every copy of it is byte-identical. **Zero-assertion.** Generated by driving the real `_frame()` through the three states it emits — healthy, degraded, producer-failed — so a field cannot be in the contract and absent from the response. ⭐ It exists because two suites pinned the two sides and **nothing pinned them to each other**: the agent could rename a field, both stay green, and the client silently reads null. ⚑ Not hypothetical — `answers` was found carrying two different TYPES down the two producer paths on 2026-08-27, by hand, by diffing sensor output. ⚠ **A second copy lands in `agience-observe`, and that is the point**: a client repo that can only check itself when a sibling repo happens to be checked out is a client repo that stops checking. Same arrangement as `agent_instructions.py`, held the same way. `--write` regenerates |

**Never edit a baseline to make numbers go down.** A baseline may only shrink by fixing what it
counts. Re-pinning is a deliberate act that arrives with written reasons.

A NEW invariant is pinned at what it MEASURES on the day it lands, never at a figure quoted from an
earlier pass. `data_integrity_check.versions_whose_root_is_missing` was first written as 4,074 from
an audit hours old and measured 4,087 on introduction; pinning below the truth ships a gate that is
red on arrival and teaches everyone to ignore it.

## Agent instructions are generated

`AGENTS.md` at a repo root is the **source**, and the only one to edit. `CLAUDE.md` and
`.github/copilot-instructions.md` are generated from it plus this shared file:

    python agience-cloud/deploy/agent_instructions.py            # check for drift
    python agience-cloud/deploy/agent_instructions.py --write     # regenerate
    python agience-cloud/deploy/agent_instructions.py --list      # coverage

Editing a generated copy loses the edit on the next run. Move it into `AGENTS.md` instead.

## The memory lane (Mantle)

Claude Code recalls context before every prompt and captures prose and transcripts, through
`~/.claude/hooks/`, against **`https://mantle.home.agience.ai`** (node `71/home`).

- Switch nodes **only** with `python ~/.claude/hooks/mantle_target.py <name>` — it writes both the
  hook half and the MCP half. Editing one by hand gives a session that recalls from one store and
  writes to another, with no error on either side.
- `python ~/.claude/hooks/mantle_hook_health.py` says whether the lane is actually working. Run it
  before concluding the store is empty: a recall that overran its timeout logs the same `no-hits`
  as one that genuinely found nothing.
- **Lane discipline.** Claude Code's own `MEMORY.md` holds preferences and working feedback; Mantle
  holds work products. Never write the same fact to both.

## Conventions that bite

- **Some Python sources here carry a UTF-8 BOM, and it is long-standing.** Read Python with `utf-8-sig`, never bare `utf-8`: the BOM survives as U+FEFF, `ast.parse` raises, and a tool that swallows the exception skips the file in silence. Measured 2026-08-26 — it cost a gate a fifth of the files it believed it was reading, including a served surface's entry point and six of its routers, while reporting green. They are NOT being stripped: the tooling fix is one word and the churn would touch several repos for no other gain. A sweep that cannot read a file must SAY SO — `N found` and `N found, k unreadable` are different claims. See `agience-build/tighten/STATE.json`, the BOM findings.
- `node.env` is committed and carries no credential. `.env` beside it is gitignored. That split is
  what makes configuration reviewable.
- A `_`-prefixed repo is a **working tree, not a product**: `_scratch`, `_archive`, `_fleet`.
- `_secret/` has no `.git`, and that absence is the whole protection.
- **`_ci-work/` MOVED OUT of this root on 2026-08-26 and is now a sibling of the workspace, not
  a member of it.** It is CI's own clone of EVERY repo, written by the post-receive hook. Measured
  2026-08-25: 242 MB, a full clone of all 20 repos each with its own `.git`, written by CI within
  the minute. A grep, audit or gate that did not exclude it counted every file in the workspace
  **twice**, and the duplicates look exactly like the shadow implementations a cleanup pass exists
  to find. Being *"outside every repo"* was true and bought nothing — nothing at this root is a
  repo. Being outside the WORKSPACE is what stops a sweep reaching it, because every sweep here
  starts at this root.
  **Keep it in your prune set anyway.** `ci_runner --work` can still place a tree inside, and
  `_archive/` holds an older `_ci-work/` that is still here. Neither is a workspace member; both are
  scratch belonging to something else.
- Git across the whole workspace is `./git-all.sh` from `agience-build`: `status` · `add .` ·
  `commit -m` · `push` · `pull`. It replaced the old push-all and pull-all shims on 2026-08-24 —
  those names are gone, not aliased, and are left unbackticked here because they no longer
  resolve to a file. `push` defaults to the NAS, **not** GitHub — the NAS
  bares carry the post-receive hook that triggers CI.
- A subset is `--only <glob>`, never a second manifest.

## Do not, unless asked in those words

Commit · push · deploy · restart a service · run Docker · install packages · touch live
infrastructure · create a GitHub repo. Default to editing files and reporting what you found.

# Working in this repo

This is the Agience Mantle source repo (see README.md for the architecture: an
encrypted artifact lattice — authorization is the encryption). The `mantle`
MCP server connected in this session is a live dev instance ("71dev"), so this
project is both the thing being built and, deliberately, a dogfooding target
for its own memory/search capabilities.

## Mantle MCP vs. local memory — pick one lane per fact

Claude Code already has a free, automatic, local cross-session memory
(`~/.claude/.../memory/`) for user preferences, feedback on how to work in
this repo, and project facts. Prefer that for anything Claude-Code-specific —
it costs nothing and is read in every session automatically.

Use the `mantle` MCP tools (`create_artifact`, `recall`, `update_artifact`,
`get_artifact`, `list_artifacts`, `delete_artifact`) instead for:

- Substantive work products worth recalling later, especially across tools
  (Copilot Chat is wired to the same server)
- Structured artifacts that benefit from tags/search/versioning
- Anything meant to exercise Mantle itself as a product

**Don't write the same fact to both stores** — that's the one place real
duplication happens.

## Cost model

- The 7 Mantle tool schemas are deferred and load into context only on first
  use, then *append* to the tool list rather than replacing it — this
  preserves Claude Code's existing prompt cache prefix, so loading them
  mid-session doesn't blow the cache. If a session never touches Mantle, it
  costs nothing.
- Prompt caching (5 min / ~1hr TTL) is entirely intra-conversation and has
  nothing to do with Mantle — it can't survive between sessions either way.
  Mantle's value is substituting one cheap `recall` call for re-deriving
  context from scratch in a new session, not interacting with the cache
  mechanism itself.
- `create_artifact`/`update_artifact` cost roughly what writing the same
  content to a file would (content is tool-call input, billed once).
  `recall` is cheap — query text in, entropy-cut previews (the densest spans
  of each hit, not a truncated prefix — see `search/beacon/density.py`;
  length isn't fixed, it's whatever the cut finds signal for) + a score out.
  Pull full content via `get_artifact` only when actually needed, not by
  default.

## Practical usage

- Always set `content_type` explicitly on `create_artifact`.
- Prefer `recall` over `list_artifacts` for finding things — `recall` scores
  relevance/coverage; `list_artifacts` only pages in id/recency order and
  matches nothing.
- `recall` supports `field:value` filters (`title:`, `tags:`, `content_type:`,
  `created_at:`, etc.) — use them before falling back to free text.
